title: Лебедь, Щука и Рак
author: Иван Крылов
summary: Three creatures harness themselves to one cart and pull three ways. Complete fable in verse.

source.editionId: Krylov, Басни, Книга четвёртая, V; Wikisource revision 4796646

rights.original: Krylov (died 1844); underlying Russian work first published in 1816 and public domain.
rights.transcription: Russian transcription from Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA; source page links to its revision history and terms.
rights.translation: New English translation for Slovarchik, CC BY-SA 4.0; no published translation reused.

translationReview.method: Checked all 13 verse lines against the pinned source, taking the printed text and not the manuscript variants recorded in its footnotes. Kept the closing line as a statement of fact, since «воз и ныне там» became a proverb from it.

sentences.ru:
Когда в товарищах согласья нет,
На лад их дело не пойдет,
И выйдет из него не дело, только мука.
sentences.en:
When there is no agreement among companions,
Their business will not go smoothly,
And nothing will come of it but torment.

sentences.ru:
Однажды Лебедь, Рак, да Щука
Везти с поклажей воз взялись,
И вместе трое все в него впряглись;
Из кожи лезут вон, а возу все нет ходу!
sentences.en:
One day a Swan, a Crayfish and a Pike
Undertook to draw a loaded cart,
And all three harnessed themselves to it together;
They strain for all they are worth, and still the cart will not move!

sentences.ru:
Поклажа бы для них казалась и легка:
Да Лебедь рвётся в облака,
Рак пятится назад, а Щука тянет в воду.
sentences.en:
The load would have seemed light enough for them:
But the Swan strains up into the clouds,
The Crayfish backs away, and the Pike pulls towards the water.

sentences.ru:
Кто виноват из них, кто прав, — судить не нам;
Да только воз и ныне там.
sentences.en:
Which of them is at fault and which is right is not for us to judge;
Only the cart is standing there to this day.
